reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it provides an operational tutorial for submitting an existing token balance through a platform's exchange and mining menus. Although the interface displays account balances, bonuses and a token submission transaction, the supplied content does not make a concrete deceptive earnings promise, request credentials or sensitive data, or show payment for mining participation.

citations.quote: This is one coin tutorial on mining your one coins using your tokens.
Let's go ahead and mine. We are going to click on exchange here on left hand menu

opening.argument: The video links a concrete platform action to an apparent token reward. It instructs viewers to submit their token balance for mining, then presents the result as a token-doubling mechanism. The transaction history reinforces that linkage: an outgoing submission is followed by two incoming entries labeled as bonuses. That is more than a generic discussion of cryptocurrency; it is an operational pathway in which viewers surrender tokens through the platform in expectation of additional tokens. The tutorial framing makes the process appear routine and accessible, while the promised outcome is represented through the platform's own balance and transaction displays.

citations.quote: we have 10 000 tokens here and we want to start mining those so we can put them over here into one coins.
what we do now here is put in the number of tokens that we have to submit.
token double

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling this an operational tutorial does not answer what the operation is designed to induce. The video explicitly directs submission of tokens and describes a doubling outcome, while the displayed history pairs the outgoing submission with bonus credits. The absence of a spoken request for credentials or a cash deposit does not remove the asset-transfer and reward relationship that the viewer is being shown.

citations.quote: what we do now here is put in the number of tokens that we have to submit.
token double

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The quoted instructions show only that an existing balance is submitted inside the demonstrated platform; they do not establish a free reward, guaranteed doubling, or a solicitation to pay. The phrase “token double” is an incomplete transcription fragment, and the transaction display shows labels and balances, not proof that viewers receive spendable assets or that the process is deceptive. A tutorial can demonstrate an interface without making a scam promise.

citations.quote: This is one coin tutorial on mining your one coins using your tokens.
Once the page refreshes you'll see this, but this is not accurate.
Subscribe to the channel and review more videos.

opening.argument: Several concrete warning signals appear together. The interface displays a substantial token balance, asks the user to submit that balance, and records an outgoing transaction at a stated difficulty. It then displays incoming “Split bonus” entries, creating the appearance that submission produces additional assets. The narrator also says the page may initially be inaccurate and that viewers should not worry if changes do not appear immediately, which normalizes a delay between the action and the supposed result. Taken together, the system presents a high-friction asset submission, a technical-sounding condition, bonus credits, and delayed confirmation as one apparently easy mining opportunity.

citations.quote: Don't worry if you don't see the changes immediately.
You will see here in green, submit OK.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The interface is not neutral evidence merely because it looks like a dashboard. It shows a user being asked to submit tokens under a difficulty condition and then displays bonus entries, while the narration preemptively explains away delayed or inaccurate results. Those features are precisely the kind of presentation that can make an unsupported reward mechanism seem credible, even without an explicit cash-payment request.

citations.quote: Don't worry if you don't see the changes immediately.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: These details show interface behavior, not deception. The warning that the page may update later expressly cautions viewers that the display is not immediately accurate, rather than guaranteeing a return. “Split bonus” is a platform label visible in a transaction history, but neither the label nor the mining screen proves that the bonus is real, withdrawable, or promised to viewers. No supplied evidence shows urgency, payment, or a fabricated guarantee.

citations.quote: but this is not accurate. The system now needs to update.
You will see here in green, submit OK.

opening.argument: Although presented as instruction, the video functions as promotion by walking viewers through the exact participation path: locate the exchange, open mining, enter the token amount, agree, and submit. The title frames the activity as a way to mine tokens for OneCoin, while the demonstration emphasizes the apparent token balance and bonus outcome. This does not merely explain what a platform contains; it reduces the viewer's uncertainty about how to participate and portrays the submission as successful. The practical effect is to steer viewers toward committing tokens to the platform under the appeal of receiving more.

citations.quote: How Do I Mine My Tokens For OneCoin
Let's go ahead and mine. We are going to click on exchange here on left hand menu
Now what we want to do is click on submit We're going to agree.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The step-by-step format is itself the promotional mechanism: viewers are shown where to click, what amount to enter, and how to approve submission. Describing the content as education overlooks that the lesson culminates in committing tokens and presents the resulting bonus entries as evidence that participation works. A disclaimer-free walkthrough can solicit participation without using the word “buy.”

citations.quote: Now what we want to do is click on submit We're going to agree.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The steps establish only that the video demonstrates navigation through an exchange and mining interface. The title and tutorial language do not promise a return, and the supplied description merely asks viewers to subscribe and review more videos. The displayed transaction history cannot by itself show that the presenter is soliciting participation or that any bonus is genuine, withdrawable, or deceptive.
